item.title: Programa espacial europeu Ariane recebe apoio da Amazon
item.description: A Amazon Leo encomendou mais seis lançamentos do foguete europeu Ariane 6, informou a operadora Arianespace nesta quarta-feira, dando um impulso ao principal programa espacial da Europa.
item.dc:creator: Tim Hepher, Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: A Amazon Leo (AMZN.O) encomendou mais seis lançamentos do foguete europeu Ariane 6, informou a operadora Arianespace nesta quarta-feira, dando um impulso ao principal programa espacial da Europa. O anúncio, feito em um encontro em Paris eleva para 24 o número de lançamentos do Ariane encomendados pela Amazon até 2031. Os novos voos começarão na versão Ariane 64 de alta capacidade em 2029, disse o braço comercial do ArianeGroup (AIR.PA) (SAF.PA) . O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, elogiou o acordo na abertura de uma cúpula espacial de dois dias, evitada pelas principais empresas espaciais norte-americanas, incluindo a Blue Origin, provedora de lançamentos de propriedade do fundador da Amazon, Jeff Bezos, após o que fontes descreveram na semana passada como pressão da Casa Branca sobre a agenda da cúpula, liderada pela Europa. A Amazon pretende fornecer internet de banda larga globalmente com sua rede de milhares de satélites planejados em órbita baixa da Terra, desafiando a Starlink da SpaceX (SPCX.O) , que acumulou milhões de clientes em todo o mundo. A Amazon tem dependido principalmente do foguete Atlas V da United Launch Alliance, empreendimento conjunto de foguetes da Boeing (BA.N) e da Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , para levar seus satélites ao espaço. O acordo de quarta-feira demonstra uma crescente dependência do principal lançador europeu, visto que o fornecimento norte-americano enfrenta escassez, embora a atividade de lançamento europeia continue insignificante em comparação com a SpaceX de Elon Musk. A Arianespace colocou 100 satélites Amazon Leo em órbita em três missões Ariane 6 neste ano. A Amazon tinha anteriormente uma exigência regulatória para lançar metade de seus 3.232 satélites iniciais até o verão (do hemisfério norte), mas essa exigência foi dispensada em junho depois que a empresa alegou escassez de suprimentos. A Arianespace afirmou na quarta-feira que anunciaria outros novos negócios, elevando o número de lançamentos adicionais para 10. Atualmente, a empresa possui encomendas para cerca de 30 lançamentos, com vagas disponíveis em 2029 e 2030, segundo um porta-voz.

item.title: The Gulf of uncertainty
item.description: How many times can we ask whether the Middle East war has entered a new, more dangerous phase?
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills
item.content:encoded: How many times can we ask whether the Middle East war has entered a new, more dangerous phase? In the [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"biggest wave of attacks on commercial shipping"] since the war began, Iran said on Wednesday it struck 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz after the United States sank five Iranian oil tankers. A tanker carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil caught fire after a drone strike, merchant ships were reported hit across the Gulf and Gulf of Oman, and Brent crude surged above $100 a barrel for the first time since July. The rhetoric has escalated too. Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned that if the enemy strikes two or three Iranian targets, Tehran would respond by hitting 20, while signalling plans for a much larger maritime exclusion zone. At the same time, a second front is heating up. The most serious Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia since the 2022 truce left dozens wounded and oil facilities ablaze, raising fresh concerns about the security of Gulf shipping and energy infrastructure far beyond Hormuz. This week, Gulf Currents examines what happens when instability stops just being a risk and becomes a constant. We look at how a half-year security crisis is reshaping decision-making across the Gulf, how uncertainty is becoming the region's new normal, and what that means for economies built on a reputation for stability. We also round up the latest developments on the military front and highlight a Reuters investigation into how two Israeli brothers are helping drive the expansion of West Bank settler outposts. NEWS BRIEFING A [USN:S8N44U031 TEXT:"tanker carrying about 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil"] was struck by a drone in Iraqi territorial waters on Wednesday, sparking a fire, with no crew casualties reported. Several other merchant vessels in the Gulf were also hit by disabling fire overnight, as Iran said it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday they had captured a [USN:L1N4500TB TEXT:"U.S. uncrewed submarine drone"] at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, offering a rare glimpse into how underwater drones are being used in military operations. The Pentagon said it was an “older model” Anduril Dive-LD drone, carrying no sensitive data, which had malfunctioned. Saudi Arabia [USN:S8N44U033 TEXT:"lifted an alert"] in the southern city of Khamis Mushait after Houthi attacks there and in three other nearby cities wounded 73 people and set oil installations ablaze. It was the most significant Houthi-Saudi escalation since a 2022 truce, coming against the backdrop of a recent Houthi Red Sea blockade and Saudi-backed offensives on Houthi territory. Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported at least 21 killed in Saudi strikes on Al Jawf, Yemen. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed carrying out strikes there. THE GULF OF UNCERTAINTY For three decades, the Gulf ran on a quiet confidence you could feel in the smallest details: front doors left unlocked, empty cars idling outside a supermarket, a sense of security so complete it became invisible. Oil and gas flowed, capital followed, and people came from every corner of the world, drawn by opportunity, good money and a life that felt safe. It was, for a generation, the region's great certainty – a sure bet that few thought to question.  Then came the war, followed by something harder to name: a fuzzy zone that is neither fully war nor fully peace. In August, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash captured the mood in a post on X: "The region cannot remain in a state of neither war nor peace indefinitely; its stability and the future of its people demand clarity of vision and direction."  He wasn't describing a crisis with an end date. He was describing a condition — one where the next phase "cannot be built on fragile foundations or arrangements” disconnected from international law, peaceful coexistence, respect for sovereignty and the logic of peace. That distinction matters for the future of the Gulf. There's a difference between risk — things you can price, like ordinary swings in oil prices — and true uncertainty, where nobody can calculate the odds because nobody can even define the variables. Will the Strait of Hormuz fully reopen? Nobody knows. And, as [USN:L6N4500W5 TEXT:"Reuters energy columnist Ron Bousso"] has put it, uncertainty itself has become a fundamental in the oil market. Fear is being priced in — as a premium quietly built into everything from grocery costs to hiring decisions to government budgets. These days, it’s in small print everywhere. The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's own registration page for its Doha meeting later this month, for example, reassures participants it is "committed to delivering a successful gathering". But it also notes that organisers are "maintaining appropriate contingency arrangements" and that "final decisions will be taken nearer the time." The bank’s annual meeting now comes with an asterisk. Which raises an uncomfortable question: was the Gulf's 30-year certainty ever real — or a confidence trick the region needed to tell itself, and the world, to keep the money and people coming? Perhaps this isn't a deviation from the norm. Perhaps it's a correction to it. What happens next will show up in ordinary decisions: whether a company delays a hire, whether a family books a holiday without worrying the airspace might close, whether a government's budget cuts stay modest or turn deep enough to undo years of growth. Multiply enough of those choices, and uncertainty in the Gulf stops being a mood. As with the oil market, it becomes a new fundamental. CHART OF THE WEEK Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since July 24 as escalating attacks in the Middle East, including on tankers, stifled hopes of a normalisation of oil shipping in the region. The move brought futures prices into line with physical crude and fuel markets, where prices have already been trading above the psychological threshold. Front-month Brent crude futures were up $2.74, or 2.8%, at $100.66 a barrel by 1315 GMT, after earlier touching $100.95. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was up $2.74, or 3%, at $95.77 a barrel, its highest level since early June. [USN:P8N43I0BY TEXT:"Read more from Anushree Ashish Mukherjee and Robert Harvey."] EXCERPT: How two Israeli brothers are driving a West Bank settler land grab From a hilltop sprawl of industrial buildings, a family of Israeli settlers is cranking out prefabricated buildings to accelerate the expansion of illegal Jewish outposts in the occupied West Bank, driving Palestinians from their homes. Libi Construction and Infrastructure, owned by brothers Eliav and Harel ‘Coco’ Libi, is building a new factory to produce the simple white structures they and others install in outposts, Eliav Libi said in an April social-media post. Seen one recent day from a nearby road, the company’s compound had at least five warehouses, flanked by rows of prefabricated houses and stacks of building material. Excavators worked to expand the site, which is in the settlement of Shilo. The Libi operation reflects a growing settlement strategy to claim expanses of West Bank land quickly and cheaply. Instead of building modern complexes and neighborhoods, with Israeli government permits, these outposts often start with one or two prefabricated houses and no legal approval. They’re occupied by young Israeli herders who bring livestock to graze land used by Palestinian shepherds and farmers. All Israeli settlements are widely condemned by the United Nations and many European countries, among others. Outposts like those founded by the Libis are illegal even under Israeli law, which requires advance approval to build in areas of the West Bank under Israeli administrative control. Yet the brothers receive broad Israeli government support as they race to expand.

item.title: Cowboys place G Tyler Smith (thumb) on IR
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys placed three-time Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith on injured reserve Wednesday, sidelining him a minimum of four games.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Cowboys placed three-time Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith on injured reserve Wednesday, sidelining him a minimum of four games. The move was expected for Smith, who reportedly could miss as many as six games after undergoing thumb surgery. T.J. Bass is expected to start in his place at left guard. The Cowboys signed Nick Leverett off their practice squad to the 53-man roster. Fellow guard Laken Tomlinson, a former first-round pick of the Detroit Lions, was signed to their practice squad. Smith, 25, has started 63 regular-season games since being selected by Dallas with the No. 24 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. He has been named to the Pro Bowl in each of the last three seasons. Leverett, 29, played in one game off the bench for the Cowboys last season. He has appeared in 23 career games (11 starts) since 2021 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New England Patriots, Arizona Cardinals and Cowboys. Tomlinson, 34, played in 10 games (seven starts) with the Houston Texans last season. He made the Pro Bowl with the San Francisco 49ers in 2021 and has appeared in 173 games (162 starts) with the Lions, 49ers, New York Jets, Seattle Seahawks and Texans. --Field Level Media

item.title: Festival de Cinema de Toronto busca atrair público mais jovem com estreias de filmes independentes
item.description: O Festival Internacional de Cinema de Toronto (TIFF) tem como objetivo atrair um público mais jovem, interessado principalmente em obras fora do mainstream de Hollywood, voltando o foco para filmes independentes, afirmou a diretora de programação do festival.
item.dc:creator: Bhargav Acharya
item.content:encoded: O Festival Internacional de Cinema de Toronto (TIFF) tem como objetivo atrair um público mais jovem, interessado principalmente em obras fora do mainstream de Hollywood, voltando o foco para filmes independentes, afirmou a diretora de programação do festival. O festival retorna para sua 51ª edição na quinta-feira com cerca de 300 filmes, em um momento em que os filmes de grande orçamento apoiados pelos estúdios ficaram em segundo plano, assim como aconteceu em Veneza e Cannes este ano. “Acho que, para nós, como festival, estamos realmente observando uma mudança demográfica muito significativa, com o público mais jovem voltando ao cinema e buscando ativamente conteúdos e experiências cinematográficas que vão além das ofertas convencionais”, afirmou Anita Lee, diretora de programação do TIFF, à Reuters. Lee disse que o TIFF quer “aproveitar o momento” com esse foco. “Acho que isso também atrai um público mais jovem que está amadurecendo como um público global, muito mais familiarizado... com filmes e cinema de todo o mundo”, declarou ela. Entre os filmes que estreiam no festival estão “Rescue”, um documentário de Sine Plambech que explora a crise imigratória no Mediterrâneo, e “Tehran, Under the Skin”, de Afsaneh Salari, que aborda a indústria da beleza no Irã, mesmo em meio a um conflito com EUA e Israel. O documentário de longa duração de Alex Gibney sobre o homem mais rico do mundo, Elon Musk, que estreou no Festival de Cinema de Veneza, fará sua estreia na América do Norte. Musk tem cidadania canadense. Lee está ansiosa pela estreia canadense de “Elsinore”, em que Andrew Scott retrata a luta do falecido ator escocês Ian Charleson contra a Aids. A estreia mundial de “Eu Sou o Rocky”, do diretor Peter Farrelly — que recria a história de como Sylvester Stallone conseguiu que o filme homônimo fosse produzido —, e o lançamento norte-americano do drama “Amor Possível”, do diretor sul-coreano Lee Chang-dong, também são muito aguardados, disse ela. O festival estenderá o tapete vermelho para estrelas como Penélope Cruz, Seth Rogen, Naomi Watts, Courteney Cox e Helen Mirren. O TIFF escolheu “A Arte de Ser Heumann”, da diretora vencedora do Oscar Sian Heder, como filme de abertura, estrelado por Ruth Madeley no papel da ativista pelos direitos das pessoas com deficiência Judy Heumann. O festival de 11 dias terminará em 20 de setembro.

item.title: Drones hit Russia's gas hinterland in northern Siberia for the first time
item.description: An industrial facility caught fire in Novy Urengoy, a gas-producing city in northern Russia, following a drone attack, regional Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said on Wednesday, in the first such attack on the country's natural gas hinterland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An industrial facility caught fire in Novy Urengoy, a gas-producing city in northern Russia, following a drone attack, regional Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said on Wednesday, in the first such attack on the country's natural gas hinterland. Artyukhov did not identify the facility involved. "Most importantly, there were no fatalities or injuries. The extent and nature of the damage are being determined," he said on the Telegram messaging app. Russia's energy company Gazprom did not reply to a request to comment about the attack on the region, some 3,000 km (1,800 miles) from the Ukrainian border. Novy Urengoy is Russia's unofficial gas capital, located in the Yamal-Nenets region in northern Western Siberia. Gazprom used to export gas from Yamal as far as Western Europe until the ties broke down following the start of Russia's war in Ukraine in 2022. It estimated the region's gas resources at 26.5 trillion cubic metres as of 2020, enough to cover global demand for more than six years.

item.title: Legal AI startup Harvey reaches $15.5 billion valuation in new funding round
item.description: Legal software startup Harvey said on Wednesday that it raised $550 million at a $15.5 billion valuation in a funding round co-led by new investors Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Legal software startup Harvey said on Wednesday that it raised $550 million at a $15.5 billion valuation in a funding round co-led by new investors Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Here are the details: The San Francisco-based company said the latest round will "accelerate Harvey’s efforts to help law firms, in-house legal teams, and professional services firms build and own their intelligence at scale." Harvey develops legal AI tools for law firms and corporate legal departments, helping automate legal workflows such as contract analysis, due diligence, compliance and litigation. Reuters' parent company Thomson Reuters also sells AI-assisted research tools for the legal industry. Existing Harvey investors Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, a16z, Coatue, Conviction, Elad Gil, Evantic, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Verified Capital and WNDR participated in the latest round, in addition to new investors Diffusion, Lightspeed, Sapphire Ventures and Whale Rock, Harvey said. Harvey also said on Wednesday that it has acquired San Francisco-based startup Guardrails AI, an AI security platform for agents, in its fourth acquisition this year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. [USN:L4N40D14A TEXT:"Harvey raised"] $200 million at an $11 billion valuation in March. The company said it is used by 80% of the 100 highest grossing firms in the United States. Legal tech companies have attracted millions from investors that see the promise in AI to speed up and reshape lawyers’ work. Legora [USN:L8N3ZY16Z TEXT:"raised"] $550 million at a $5.55 billion valuation in March and Clio [USN:L4N3WM0ZY TEXT:"raised"] $500 million at a $5 billion valuation in November. A new venture capital fund with backing from a group of corporate general counsels and law firm Wilson Sonsini [USN:L6N4500YH TEXT:"launched"] on Tuesday to invest in early-stage legal, regulatory and compliance tech startups.

item.title: Brennan rules Seville sprint as Visma claim seventh Vuelta stage win
item.description: Matthew Brennan turned Seville's grand avenues into another Visma-Lease a Bike runway on Wednesday, powering to his fifth stage win of this year's Vuelta a Espana as the Dutch team's remarkable run of success continued.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Matthew Brennan turned Seville's grand avenues into another Visma-Lease a Bike runway on Wednesday, powering to his fifth stage win of this year's Vuelta a Espana as the Dutch team's remarkable run of success continued. The 21-year-old Briton, making his debut in the race, again proved untouchable when the peloton wound up for the final sprint, beating Jordi Meeus into second place while Magnus Cort Nielsen finished third. Visma have now won seven stages in the race, with Brennan's five victories added to Wout van Aert's two, underlining their dominance of the Vuelta's flat and rolling stages. Enzo Paleni, Sinuhe Fernandez and Fredrik Dversnes attacked shortly after the start of the 185-km stage, although Dversnes quickly dropped back. Paleni and Fernandez pressed on and built a lead of more than five minutes around the halfway mark. Visma, driven for long spells by Steven Kruijswijk, kept the breakaway within reach, with Cofidis also contributing as they worked for Bryan Coquard. A brief acceleration by Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe split the bunch inside the final 50 kilometres, but the peloton soon regrouped. Paleni and Fernandez still held a lead of 1:50 with 25 kilometres remaining before Fernandez took the intermediate sprint at San Jose de la Rinconada. Paleni then attacked alone with 15 kilometres left, but his lead shrank rapidly and he was caught inside the final three kilometres. UAE, INEOS and Uno-X all tried to shape the run-in, but Brennan timed his effort best to seal another emphatic win. Overall leader Enric Mas finished safely in the bunch to retain the red jersey for a ninth successive stage, leading Felix Gall by 2:06 and Primoz Roglic by 2:10.

item.title: Clay valued at $7.1 billion in latest funding round as AI agent startups run hot
item.description: Software startup Clay, whose AI tools help automate sales and marketing tasks, said on Wednesday it raised $115 million at a $7.1 billion valuation, more than twice as much as it was valued a year ago, as investors pile into companies developing AI agents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Software startup Clay, whose AI tools help automate sales and marketing tasks, said on Wednesday it raised $115 million at a $7.1 billion valuation, more than twice as much as it was valued a year ago, as investors pile into companies developing AI agents. The New York-based company, whose customers include Google and Anthropic, develops AI agents that analyze business data to help sales teams decide what to do next and execute those actions. Here are more details: The Series D funding round was led by Wellington, with participation from Sequoia, StepStone, Andreessen Horowitz and Perennial among others. "AI is unleashing the biggest wave of company creation in history, and Clay's goal is to be the engine those companies use to grow to their full potential," said Kareem Amin, co-founder and CEO of Clay. "We started by aggregating the best data for B2B companies. Then we built the infrastructure to run any personalized campaign on top of it. Now we're building agents that can help grow your company for you," he added. Founded in 2017, Clay was valued at [USN:L4N3TX17T TEXT:"$3.1 billion"] in August 2025 when it raised $100 million in a funding round led by CapitalG.

item.title: Israël ordonne à la GB de fermer son consulat de Jérusalem-Est d'ici un mois
item.description: Israël a ordonné à Londres de fermer son consulat de Jérusalem-Est dans un délai d’un mois, ont déclaré mercredi des responsables israéliens, une mesure décidée en représailles aux sanctions annoncées la veille par le Royaume-Uni, avec d'autres pays dont la France, contre les colonies israéliennes de Cisjordanie occupée.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Israël a ordonné à Londres de fermer son consulat de Jérusalem-Est dans un délai d’un mois, ont déclaré mercredi des responsables israéliens, une mesure décidée en représailles aux sanctions annoncées la veille par le Royaume-Uni, avec d'autres pays dont la France, contre les colonies israéliennes de Cisjordanie occupée. Outre la demande de fermeture du consulat, [USN:L8N45010Q TEXT:"Israël a interdit"] l'entrée de son territoire à douze responsables politiques britanniques, ordonné aux responsables et diplomates britanniques présents en Cisjordanie de partir, et déclaré que la Grande-Bretagne ne pouvait plus former les forces de sécurité palestiniennes en Cisjordanie. Les sanctions prévoient des restrictions sur les importations de produits issus de Cisjordanie occupée. Elles comptent parmi les mesures collectives les plus sévères prises par les principaux alliés occidentaux d’Israël en réponse à l’expansion des colonies en Cisjordanie et à la recrudescence des violences commises par les colons à l’encontre des Palestiniens. Le ministre israélien des Affaires étrangères, Gideon Sa'ar, a déclaré sur X qu’il avait remercié Kemi Badenoch, la présidente du Parti conservateur britannique, pour ses critiques contre les sanctions, notamment ses propos dans The Sun, où elle affirme que le gouvernement travailliste fait "passer ses propres intérêts partisans avant l’intérêt national". Si l’effet de ces sanctions est essentiellement symbolique, elles soulignent l’isolement croissant de l'État hébreu parmi les pays qu’il considérait autrefois comme des alliés proches.

item.title: Comercio mundial de mercancías se fortalece a pesar de aranceles y tensiones en Oriente Medio: OMC
item.description: El comercio mundial de mercancías se ha fortalecido desde junio a pesar de las incertidumbres geopolíticas y relacionadas con las políticas, informó el miércoles la Organización Mundial del Comercio, lo que pone de manifiesto la resistencia de los flujos de mercancías, aunque los riesgos siguen siendo elevados.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: El comercio mundial de mercancías se ha fortalecido desde junio a pesar de las incertidumbres geopolíticas y relacionadas con las políticas, informó el miércoles la Organización Mundial del Comercio, lo que pone de manifiesto la resistencia de los flujos de mercancías, aunque los riesgos siguen siendo elevados. La lectura de septiembre del barómetro de la OMC, que mide el crecimiento del comercio de mercancías, fue de 102, lo que supone una mejora respecto al 101,7 registrado en junio, y el crecimiento se mantiene por encima de la tendencia. La OMC publica su Barómetro del Comercio de Mercancías cuatro veces al año. Este abarca los pedidos de exportación, el transporte aéreo de mercancías, el transporte marítimo en contenedores, los productos de automoción, las materias primas y los componentes electrónicos. Las lecturas superiores a 100 indican un crecimiento por encima de la tendencia de referencia de 100, mientras que las cifras inferiores a 100 apuntan a un crecimiento por debajo de la tendencia. El organismo comercial con sede en Ginebra señaló que este fortalecimiento se produjo a pesar de la incertidumbre vinculada a las tensiones geopolíticas y a la evolución de las políticas comerciales. En marzo, la OMC pronosticó que el crecimiento del comercio mundial de mercancías se ralentizaría notablemente hasta el 1,9% este año, frente al 4,6% de 2025, y que podría desacelerarse aún más si la guerra de Estados Unidos con Irán sigue haciendo subir los precios de la energía y perturbando el transporte mundial. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha impuesto aranceles generalizados a sus socios comerciales de todo el mundo, mientras que el tráfico marítimo a través del estratégico estrecho de Ormuz —por donde solía transitar una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo— se ha visto gravemente afectado por el conflicto en Oriente Medio. Sin embargo, la fuerte demanda de componentes electrónicos vinculada a la inversión en inteligencia artificial e infraestructura digital estaba ayudando a contrarrestar los efectos negativos de esos factores, según el informe de la OMC. El crecimiento del comercio sigue siendo desigual entre sectores y regiones, y la OMC advirtió de que los riesgos geopolíticos y relacionados con las políticas siguen ensombreciendo las perspectivas debido a las continuas perturbaciones en las cadenas de suministro, las rutas marítimas y los costos de transporte.

item.title: France-Schneider Electric va fermer une usine dans la Vienne, investir 150 millions d'euros
item.description: Schneider Electric prévoit d’investir 150 millions d'euros en France et de fermer une usine dans le cadre d'un plan visant à améliorer sa compétitivité dans l’Hexagone, a annoncé mercredi le groupe industriel français.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) prévoit d’investir 150 millions d'euros en France et de fermer une usine dans le cadre d'un plan visant à améliorer sa compétitivité dans l’Hexagone, a annoncé mercredi le groupe industriel français. Selon les propos d’un porte-parole du groupe à Reuters, Schneider Electric prévoit de fermer son usine de Chasseneuil-du-Poitou (Vienne) d'ici mars 2028, et de réallouer les activités du site à d'autres usines, principalement à Dijon (Côte-d'Or). "Pour les 145 collaborateurs (du site de Chasseneuil-du-Poitou) maintenant, on va commencer une phase de négociation, (...) et ça sera discuté au cas par cas", a déclaré le porte-parole, ajoutant que le reclassement au sein de l’entreprise serait une priorité. Dans le cadre de son plan, Schneider Electric va également construire un nouveau site à Évreux (Eure), qui regroupera les compétences en matière de production et de recherche et développement de ses trois sites normands existants. Si Schneider opère sur des segments de marché bénéficiant d’une croissance soutenue liée aux projets d’électrification et de digitalisation, l’entreprise est également confrontée à une saturation des volumes sur ses marchés industriels, a précisé la société. "Les ambitions, c'est de gagner en compétitivité sur des marchés pour lesquels aujourd'hui il y a une très forte pression sur les prix," a déclaré le porte-parole du groupe.

item.title: Death and illness aren't fun to talk about. Ignoring them costs more
item.description: Death and illness are not topics people like to discuss with their loved ones. But expecting family and friends to manage your money and make healthcare decisions when an emergency strikes is not a prudent estate plan.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Young
item.content:encoded: Death and illness are not topics people like to discuss with their loved ones. But expecting family and friends to manage your money and make healthcare decisions when an emergency strikes is not a prudent estate plan. Jay Friday, head of personal financial planning at Citizens Wealth Management, says you need just four key documents — and a will — to protect yourself. Here's what you need to do now, and why waiting could cause serious problems for your family. This interview is edited and condensed. What are the key financial documents that every American adult, regardless of age and wealth, should have? The [USN:L6N43G19E TEXT:"basics"] are the durable power of attorney , a healthcare proxy , an advance medical directive and a HIPAA release form . Those four typically cover the majority of what someone might need until they get into a much more complex scenario. And a will is also important . Why don't people have these documents in place? Number one, it's procrastination. And when it comes to basic estate planning, they think it's going to be expensive. They also don't want to think about their own mortality. It adds another layer of complexity. Why are beneficiary designations especially important? Naming beneficiaries is probably just as important as having a will, because you can avoid so many different pitfalls and delays when it comes to probate . When you're talking about a beneficiary designation, typically it's a qualified account, like a retirement or investment account, that has tax ramifications. Let's say you have kids. Sometimes a uniform split doesn't make sense when one child is extremely successful and another child might have special needs. If you have taxable and non-taxable parts of your estate, you can make sure it evens out among beneficiaries and maximizes the value economically across the entire household. How often should these documents be reviewed? Anytime there's a major life event, including birth, divorce, death or incapacity. As a best practice, review your estate plan every two to three years. How is a trusted contact different from someone who has power of attorney? Power of attorney is a legal document where you're giving someone legal authority to manage your affairs if you become incapacitated. A trusted contact is not an official title. But we use that when we're talking about somebody who is going to help you with care. Any tips on the best way to pick caregivers? The best person to manage your care from a financial perspective may not be the best person from a medical perspective. For healthcare needs, choose someone local and closer in proximity to take you to appointments with doctors. They can also provide hands-on to help you manage medication and pills. What's the most important first step for caregivers? Get organized. It sets you up to make wise decisions. If somebody is incapacitated, having wills, trusts and documents aligned is really important. Document everything you have, get it all in one place so that if something were to happen to the caregiver, there is somebody else in line to pick up the pieces. And communicate. Communication is huge and really supremely important. If you are planning to lean on somebody, make sure they're aware of it and that they're prepared to do so. Can digital vault services help organize important documents? I'm a big fan of the concept. It's a great way to let someone pick up where you leave off in a very seamless, quick way. Typically, you have everything lined up, and it's password protected, secured and encrypted. What estate-planning tools are overlooked? A revocable living trust is a really good tool when it comes to incapacity. It's very flexible. You can fund it with pretty much any asset. The person who creates the trust retains control, can serve as trustee and they have supreme control over it. And then, upon incapacity, a successor trustee can seamlessly come in and take over managing the funds, assets and affairs. You can even name powers over digital assets. Unlike a durable power of attorney that stops at death, a revocable trust becomes an irrevocable trust upon death. One of the cons is that they're more expensive. But on the flip side, it helps avoid probate. It extends beyond incapacity. It's a really good tool if you're thinking about incapacity, continuity and succession.

item.title: India looks to boost biofuel use amid rising crude supply risks
item.description: India is looking to increase its use of biofuels to strengthen energy security as disruptions to crude supplies push oil prices higher, Tarun Kapoor, an adviser in the Prime Minister's Office, said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Mayank Bhardwaj
item.content:encoded: India is looking to increase its use of biofuels to strengthen energy security as disruptions to crude supplies push oil prices higher, Tarun Kapoor, an adviser in the Prime Minister's Office, said on Wednesday. The Iran war has highlighted the difficulty of ensuring continuous crude supplies, Kapoor told an industry conference. Iran said on Wednesday it [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"attacked"] 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, in the biggest declared wave of attacks on shipping by both sides since the start of the six-month-old war. Brent crude futures [USN:L1N451087 TEXT:"breached"] $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since late July. Kapoor said India needs to use all available domestic resources to strengthen its energy security. India, the world's third-biggest oil importer and consumer, is conducting tests to blend some biofuels with diesel. It already blends ethanol with gasoline. India mainly uses corn-, rice- and sugarcane-based feedstocks to produce ethanol. New Delhi is also moving towards wider adoption of flex-fuel vehicles as it seeks to cut reliance on expensive energy imports and promote ethanol blends in gasoline. But motorists and independent analysts have expressed concerns that higher ethanol content could affect engine performance and fuel efficiency, as well as increase the risk of biofuel [USN:L4N44328T TEXT:"contamination."]

item.title: AIEA aprova resolução que encaminha Irã ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU
item.description: A diretoria da agência nuclear da ONU, composta por 35 países, aprovou uma resolução que encaminha o Irã ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU pela primeira vez em 20 anos por violar suas obrigações de não proliferação, informaram diplomatas nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A diretoria da agência nuclear da ONU, composta por 35 países, aprovou uma resolução que encaminha o Irã ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU pela primeira vez em 20 anos por violar suas obrigações de não proliferação, informaram diplomatas nesta quarta-feira. A resolução dá continuidade a uma anterior, aprovada em 12 de junho do ano passado — um dia antes de Israel iniciar os bombardeios contra as instalações nucleares do Irã, logo seguido pelos Estados Unidos —, que considerou o Irã em “descumprimento” dessas obrigações. Para encaminhar o caso ao Conselho por essa violação, era necessária outra resolução. Embora seja improvável que o Conselho de Segurança tome medidas concretas contra o Irã, uma vez que seus aliados, Rússia e China, são membros permanentes com direito a veto, a medida representa uma escalada no impasse diplomático entre o Irã e as potências ocidentais, e o Irã advertiu na segunda-feira que retaliaria caso a resolução fosse aprovada. O texto, proposto pelos Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, França e Alemanha, foi aprovado com 23 votos a favor, três contra e oito abstenções, segundo diplomatas presentes na reunião a portas fechadas da Agência Internacional de Energia Atômica. Os países que se opuseram foram Rússia, China e Níger, afirmaram eles. “(A diretoria) solicita ao diretor-geral (da AIEA) que comunique esta resolução e as resoluções adotadas anteriormente... a todos os membros da Agência, bem como ao Conselho de Segurança e à Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, de acordo com as disposições pertinentes do Estatuto da AIEA”, dizia o texto. Embora a constatação de não conformidade seja anterior à guerra entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã e diga respeito à falha do Irã em explicar os vestígios de urânio encontrados em locais não declarados — que a agência levou anos para investigar —, há agora outro impasse sobre o acesso da AIEA aos locais bombardeados por Israel e pelos Estados Unidos.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'envolée du pétrole pénalise les Bourses et propulse les rendements à la veille de la BCE
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette baisse mercredi, la flambée des prix du pétrole rognant l'appétit des investisseurs, qui craignent surtout que l'inflation ne s'installe durablement.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette baisse mercredi, la flambée des prix du pétrole rognant l'appétit des investisseurs, qui craignent surtout que l'inflation ne s'installe durablement. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a perdu 1,94% à 8.156,67 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a reculé de 1,74% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a abandonné 1,31%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a fini sur une baisse de 1,70%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) a perdu 1,42% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) a reculé de 1,48%. Les actions ont été durement touchées par l'instabilité accrue au Moyen-Orient, qui a propulsé mercredi les prix du pétrole au-dessus des 100 dollars le baril, un seuil symbolique qu'il n'avait plus franchi depuis le 24 juillet dernier. "La remontée du Brent vers les 100 dollars, puis son retour au-dessus de ce seuil, reflète un marché qui doit de plus en plus revoir son estimation de la durée pendant laquelle la crise au Moyen-Orient continuera à freiner l'offre en provenance de la région", souligne Ole Hansen, responsable de la stratégie sur les matières premières chez Saxo Bank. Le Brent , référence mondiale du marché, avance de 3,32% à 101,17 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) 3,55% à 96,33 dollars. Les cours du gaz sont également affectés par la recrudescence des tensions entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran ces dernières heures, comme en témoigne la flambée du contrat de référence néerlandais à échéance la plus proche sur le hub TTF , qui grimpe de plus de 4% à près de 80 euros par mégawattheure (MWh). Le conflit au Moyen-Orient s'intensifie une nouvelle fois et sa résolution semble s'éloigner encore davantage, l'Iran ayant attaqué des navires près d'Ormuz et une base américaine en Jordanie, en réponse à la destruction de pétroliers iraniens par Washington. L'escalade vient s'ajouter aux attaques revendiquées mardi par les Houthis dans le sud de l'Arabie saoudite. Ces nouvelles attaques surviennent alors que les investisseurs sont très attentifs à la politique monétaire : la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) annoncera très certainement une deuxième hausse de ses taux jeudi et le marché s'attend même à une troisième avant la fin de l'année, tandis que les chiffres de l'inflation attendus vendredi aux États-Unis pourraient déterminer la décision de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) la semaine prochaine. Les craintes d'inflation viennent aggraver les turbulences d'un marché obligataire déjà tendu en raison de la dette publique élevée des grandes économies et des risques budgétaires dans des pays comme la France. Dans la deuxième économie de la zone euro, les rendements des obligations d'État ont atteint ce mercredi leur plus haut niveau [USN:L8N4511AY TEXT:"depuis 2008"], lors de la crise financière mondiale. Aux Etats-Unis, les rendements ont brusquement augmenté alors même que le Trésor a apporté des précisions concernant ses rachats d'obligations destinés à maîtriser les tensions sur le marché de la dette : il rachètera jusqu'à 6 milliards de dollars d'obligations d'État à 10 et 20 ans jeudi, soit le triple du montant de sa dernière opération portant sur des titres à long terme. VALEURS Le secteur pétrolier et gazier (.SXEP) de l'indice Stoxx 600 a profité de la hausse des cours du pétrole et fini sur un gain de 0,23%, avec TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) , comme seule valeur terminant la séance dans le vert à Paris (+0,59%). Les actions du secteur du luxe ont été particulièrement touchées par les ventes, comme à chaque fois que les tensions géopolitiques menacent de compromettre leurs perspectives. De plus, LVMH (LVMH.PA) (-3,5%) et Burberry (BRBY.L) (-3,9%) ont été pénalisées par l'abaissement des recommandations de HSBC sur leurs titres respectifs, le courtier anticipant un second semestre plus modéré que le précédent. Inditex (ITX.MC) , la maison mère de Zara, a perdu 3,6%, après avoir fait état d'un bénéfice au deuxième trimestre inférieur aux attentes, malgré un bon démarrage des ventes d'automne. Fortum (FORTUM.HE) a en revanche grimpé de plus de 15%, le groupe énergétique finlandais ayant signé un contrat d'achat d'électricité à long terme avec Google. La principale filiale d'Alphabet va investir au moins 13 milliards d'euros d'IA en Finlande au cours des deux prochaines années, un projet présenté comme le plus gros investissement jamais réalisé par le groupe technologique américain en Europe. A WALL STREET A l'heure de la clôture en Europe, le Dow Jones (.DJI) perd 0,76%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) 0,48% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) 0,68%, également affecté par les cours de l'énergie. Meta (META.O) avance toutefois de près de 6% après le lancement d'un assistant IA capable d'effectuer de manière autonome, pour le compte de l'utilisateur, des tâches quotidiennes telles que l'envoi d'e-mails ou la réservation de voyages. TAUX Les rendements obligataires de la zone euro ont fortement progressé mercredi sur fond de craintes inflationnistes. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans a pris environ 7 points de base à 3,4299%, à son plus haut niveau depuis avril 2011, tandis que celui de l'obligation à deux ans a pris 6,4 points de base à 3,0442%. En France, le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans a gagné 10,9 points de base pour terminer à 4,3308%. Celui du titre à 30 ans a pris plus de 8 points de base pour finir à 5,06%. Aux Etats-Unis, le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans avance de 4,1 points de base à 4,8447%, les annonces du gouvernement américain sur les rachats d'obligations à long terme ne parvenant pas à freiner la tendance à la hausse. CHANGES Le dollar grappille 0,01% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , les investisseurs suivant de près les annonces du Trésor sur le marché obligataire. Le billet vert a été sous pression cette semaine en raison de l'appréciation rapide du yen japonais, soutenu par les paris renforcés sur les hausses de taux de la Banque du Japon (BoJ). L'euro gagne 0,05% à 1,1629 dollar . A SUIVRE LE 10 SEPTEMBRE : [USN:L8N44W14H] (Certaines données peuvent accuser un léger décalage)

item.title: 4-time Stanley Cup champion Andre Pronovost dies
item.description: Former Montreal Canadiens forward Andre Pronovost, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, died on Tuesday at age 90.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Montreal Canadiens forward Andre Pronovost, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, died on Tuesday at age 90. He helped the Canadiens capture the Stanley Cup in each of his first four seasons in the NHL (1956-57 to 1959-60). Pronovost posted 198 points (94 goals, 104 assists) and 405 penalty minutes in 557 career games with the Canadiens, Boston Bruins, Detroit Red Wings and Minnesota North Stars. He is the grandfather of New Jersey Devils forward Anthony Mantha. --Field Level Media

item.title: US states sue Trump administration for weakening endangered species protections
item.description: U.S. states filed two lawsuits on Wednesday accusing President Donald Trump's administration of illegally weakening the federal Endangered Species Act, a landmark law that has shielded the bald eagle and other wildlife from dangers posed by development.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: U.S. states filed two lawsuits on Wednesday accusing President Donald Trump's administration of illegally weakening the federal Endangered Species Act, a landmark law that has shielded the bald eagle and other wildlife from dangers posed by development. In one lawsuit, states challenged a rule that [USN:L1N43C0Y2 TEXT:"narrowed"] the law's definition of harm, which had long included encroachments on habitats where endangered animals live. The new rule allows oil drilling, mining and other activities in those habitats so long as those activities do not directly kill or injure the animals. The other lawsuit challenges two rules. One rule eliminates broad protections for newly threatened species unless the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service creates species-specific protections. The second rule requires the government to consider objections by developers, fossil fuel companies and other businesses before declaring areas as "critical habitats." Democratic attorneys general of 20 states and the District of Columbia joined one or both cases. The lawsuits target actions by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the National Marine Fisheries Service. Democratic-led states have filed dozens of lawsuits challenging sweeping policy changes during the second White House term of Trump, a Republican. The Fish and Wildlife Service, part of the Department of the Interior, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The fisheries service, part of the Department of Commerce, said it does not discuss pending litigation. ADMINISTRATION'S APPROACH 'EXPLOITATION,' STATE AG SAYS Enacted by Congress in 1973, the Endangered Species Act has been credited with saving animals including the California condor, grizzly bear and humpback whale from possible extinction. "The Trump administration is trying to undermine the law, the will of Congress and the will of the people who overwhelmingly support protections for endangered species," Washington Attorney General Nick Brown said at a press conference. "Instead of stewardship, this administration's approach to our land, to our water is one of exploitation." Weakening the law aligns with Trump's goal to reduce regulations that he says constrain American businesses. These include the [USN:L6N43H0T0 TEXT:"scaling back"] of a variety of environmental initiatives and standards, including by reducing government support for clean energy and repealing an Obama administration-era scientific finding that climate change threatens public health. Many wildlife advocates consider habitat loss the biggest cause of animal extinction. "We owe future generations a world where bald eagles soar, sea turtles swim and all wildlife thrives," New York Attorney General Letitia James said in a statement. INTERIOR SECRETARY HAS SAID LAW WAS 'WEAPONIZED' Interior Secretary Doug Burgum has said the Endangered Species Act has been "weaponized" to stop a myriad of projects, weakening competitiveness, undermining national security, and hurting Americans' pocketbooks. He has said the new rules more closely align the law with its original intent. The changes follow the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in 2024 to [USN:S0N3GL049 TEXT:"overrule"] a 40-year-old precedent that required courts to defer to federal agencies' reasonable interpretations of laws they administer. Wednesday's lawsuits were led by Washington State, California, Maryland and Massachusetts. Other plaintiffs include New York, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Hawaii, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Mexico, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia and Wisconsin.

item.title: Russia and Vietnam sign framework deal on strategic oil storage
item.description: Russian state-owned oil and gas company Zarubezhneft signed a framework agreement with Vietnam's state energy firm Petrovietnam on cooperation in a project to set up a strategic oil reserve in Vietnam.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian state-owned oil and gas company Zarubezhneft signed a framework agreement with Vietnam's state energy firm Petrovietnam on cooperation in a project to set up a strategic oil reserve in Vietnam. The agreement was signed during Vietnamese leader To Lam's state visit to Russia. The companies did not disclose a timeline for the project or the size of any potential strategic oil reserve. Financial terms of the agreement were also not made public. "The Russian side has proposed that its partners consider the idea of jointly establishing strategic fuel reserves in Vietnam," Russian President Vladimir Putin said in remarks after the talks. Energy cooperation has been a key focus of ties between Moscow and Hanoi. In March, Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh urged Zarubezhneft [USN:L4N40D0AX TEXT:"to increase its investment"] in Vietnam and provide long-term crude oil supplies to the Southeast Asian country, according to the Vietnamese government. In June, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Moscow was ready to support Vietnam in creating a strategic oil reserve.

item.title: Canadian dollar edges lower as trade war with US intensifies
item.description: The Canadian dollar weakened against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday as an escalating trade war between the United States and Canada offset higher oil prices, while bond yields climbed.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar weakened against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday as an escalating trade war between the United States and Canada offset higher oil prices, while bond yields climbed. The loonie was trading 0.2% lower at 1.3805 per U.S. dollar, or 72.44 U.S. cents, giving back much of the previous day's gains. It moved in a range of 1.3767 to 1.3820. The U.S. [USN:L6N4500OF TEXT:"banned"] a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import on Tuesday. The import bans came after Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods took effect after midnight on Tuesday. "Despite firmer crude oil prices, the overhang from the new retaliatory tariffs from the U.S. has dampened short-term CAD sentiment, sending the loonie lower today," said George Davis, chief technical strategist at RBC Capital Markets. Canada sends about 70% of its exports to the U.S., including oil. [USN:L1N451087 TEXT:"Brent crude futures"] breached $100 a barrel for the first time since July 24 as escalating attacks in the Middle East, including on tankers, stifled hopes of a normalization of oil shipping in the region. Elevated oil prices have raised inflation pressures globally, including in Canada. Investors have fully discounted a Bank of Canada interest rate hike by December after Governor Tiff Macklem last week said policymakers were prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high. U.S. inflation data, due on Friday, could help guide expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week. Canadian government bond yields moved higher across the curve, tracking moves in U.S. Treasuries. The 10-year was up 3.8 basis points at 3.849%, marking its highest level since May 2024.

item.title: TotalEnergies plans $10 billion Angola investment with partners over five years, CEO says
item.description: French oil major TotalEnergies will invest $10 billion with partners in Angola over the next five years to bolster production across various projects, Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanne said at an oil conference in Luanda on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Gomes
item.content:encoded: French oil major TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) will invest $10 billion with partners in Angola over the next five years to bolster production across various projects, Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanne said at an oil conference in Luanda on Wednesday. Angola, Sub-Saharan Africa's second-biggest crude oil producer after Nigeria, has undertaken a major regulatory overhaul to encourage exploration investment as it looks to maintain production levels amid mature offshore fields. TotalEnergies, the country's largest oil operator, produces around 450,000 barrels per day in Angola and is working to maintain that level, Pouyanne said, as the Southern African country strives to maintain output of around 1 million bpd. "Investments are necessary to achieve these production levels," he told delegates. TotalEnergies is developing the $6 billion Kaminho project, about 100 km (62 miles) off Angola's coast, after taking a final investment decision in 2024. Linked to the company's seventh Floating Production Storage and Offloading vessel in the country, the project in the Kwanza Basin is expected to start production in 2028. Pouyanne said on Wednesday the company had signed two new exploration licences for offshore Block 17 and Block 32 in partnership with Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) . It would also launch an artificial intelligence geoscience initiative with major companies to support exploration of Angola's offshore oil blocks. "We will apply it first to the Angolan Basin because we are convinced that there are more discoveries to be made, such as those in Block 17 and Block 0," he said.

item.title: Oito países elogiam decisão britânica de proibir importações de assentamentos ilegais na Cisjordânia

item.content:encoded: Oito países elogiaram a decisão do Reino Unido de proibir as importações provenientes de assentamentos israelenses ilegais na Cisjordânia e de impor restrições a alguns serviços, acrescentando que esperam que a medida mobilize outros países a tomar ações semelhantes. item.title: US judge urged to oust law firm Paul Weiss from sugar price-fixing case
item.description: A group of food manufacturers is urging a federal judge to bar law firm Paul Weiss from defending Domino Sugar and its owner ASR Group in a lawsuit over alleged price-fixing in the sugar industry, arguing that the firm earlier tried to represent them as plaintiffs in the case.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A group of food manufacturers is urging a federal judge to bar law firm Paul Weiss from defending Domino Sugar and its owner ASR Group in a lawsuit over alleged price-fixing in the sugar industry, arguing that the firm earlier tried to represent them as plaintiffs in the case. Kraft Heinz, Mondelēz Global, Nestlé USA, Hershey and other plaintiffs said in a filing on Tuesday in the federal court in Minnesota that they provided confidential strategy and pricing data to Paul Weiss in 2024 when they were preparing to bring the case and the law firm was vying to represent them. They asked the court to order Paul Weiss to explain why it should not be disqualified, arguing that its participation in the case creates conflicts of interest and that the firm failed to seek or obtain their consent before agreeing to represent ASR Group. According to the filing, Paul Weiss has proposed hiring separate lawyers to defend ASR against Kraft Heinz's claims specifically, because Kraft Heinz is a current client of the firm. The food manufacturers called that proposal "unworkable." Paul Weiss and a lead attorney for ASR Group at the firm, Djordje Petkoski, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. An outside lawyer for the firm in the conflict dispute also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ASR has denied the plaintiffs’ price-fixing claims. Paul Weiss in court filings has denied that its defense of ASR Group creates a conflict, arguing that the lawyers representing the company were not involved in discussions with the plaintiffs in 2024. In a letter earlier this year to the food manufacturers, Paul Weiss' general counsel Kenneth Schneider said the firm's "representation of ASR and Domino is not adverse to Kraft Heinz and is in compliance with our ethical obligations." The lead Paul Weiss attorneys who earlier sought to represent the food manufacturers, including William Isaacson, [USN:L1N3RV10O TEXT:"left the firm"] last year to open a new law firm. Paul Weiss became involved in the case as defense counsel for ASR and Domino in September last year, when Petkoski, the lead attorney for the companies, joined Paul Weiss from rival law firm A&O Shearman. Mondelēz and other plaintiffs hired law firm Jenner & Block to file their lawsuit in July against ASR Group and other sugar companies. Mondelēz and Jenner did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The case is Mondelēz Global LLC et al v. ASR Group International Inc et al, U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, No. 0:26-cv-03528. item.title: Apple eyes way to cash in on maturing iPhone users
item.description: The glory days of growth are behind, but the $4.6 trln company may find a new way to goose revenue with a foldable handset. Call it the bifocal iPhone. Millennials, the largest US generation, are just hitting the age when nearly everyone develops problems reading small text.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cyran
item.content:encoded: Apple (AAPL.O) is set to reveal its latest iPhone on Wednesday, and it’s [USN:L6N44W11I TEXT:"expected"] to be foldable. While there’s a novelty factor to an origami-style device with a typical screen for on-the-go use and a double-sized one for dedicated viewing, this is more about the $4.6 trillion company’s aging customers. It’s the modern version of bifocals. The closely watched spectacle will be the first for boss John Ternus since he took over from Tim Cook. The folding form is taking off: Samsung makes a similar product and China's Huawei and Xiaomi unveiled versions earlier this week. Apple will capture nearly a third of the market segment this year, and 40% in 2027, research outfit IDC forecasts. This spate of roll-outs relates heavily to maturity: more than 90% of Americans own a smartphone, according to Pew Research . Saturation matters for Apple: the iPhone generates over half its revenue, and is pivotal to the company's success 18 years after introducing the first model. Services now account for more than a quarter of the top line. It makes sense, therefore, to court aging buyers. When the iPhone debuted in 2007, 45% of the population was 40 or older, Census data show. Now, it’s 49%. In absolute terms, that’s 30 million more people in the range. Moreover, Millennials, or anyone born between 1981 and 1996, are the biggest U.S. generation, and just starting to hit the age when most need bifocals. An iPhone small enough to fit in a pocket with an accessible bigger screen would be useful when reading small print. Larger displays are more comfortable and allow for easier-to-read fonts. Foldables are so linked to older users that in Korea, Samsung's Galaxy versions were nicknamed "ajae," slang for an over-the-hill, un-hip man. An added bonus is that middle-aged shoppers tend to be wealthier. The new iPhone will likely cost more than $2,000. Assuming the supply chain doesn’t encounter problems, sales should be easy to spot in the upcoming holiday quarter, with or without glasses. Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky . Apple is expected to introduce a foldable iPhone with a price tag of more than $2,000 at an event on September 9, according to multiple media reports. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Porsche completes Bugatti Rimac exit, lifts 2026 cash flow outlook
item.description: Porsche said on Wednesday it had completed the sale of its stakes in Bugatti Rimac and Rimac Group after receiving regulatory approvals, finalising its exit from the Croatian electric hypercar maker and related businesses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Porsche (P911_p.DE) said on Wednesday it had completed the sale of its stakes in Bugatti Rimac and Rimac Group after receiving regulatory approvals, finalising its exit from the Croatian electric hypercar maker and related businesses. The transaction will generate proceeds of around €1 billion ($1.2 billion) for the German sports car manufacturer. The company said the deal would help lift its 2026 automotive net cash flow margin forecast to 5.5%-7.5%, from 3%-5% previously. Porsche plans to allocate €250 million of the proceeds to further fund pension obligations. The disposal forms part of Porsche's broader effort to focus on its core automotive business as the luxury carmaker faces weaker demand in China and a slower-than-expected transition to electric vehicles, issues that have pressured earnings across the European auto sector. Porsche had held a 45% stake in Bugatti Rimac and a 20.6% stake in Rimac Group after helping establish the Bugatti Rimac joint venture in 2021. Founder Mate Rimac will assume the role of president of Bugatti Automobiles as part of a management reshuffle, while former Rimac Technology executive Marko Brkljačić is expected to join the company as chief operating officer. Following the completion of the transaction, Rimac Group is set to take full control of Bugatti Rimac alongside its new investors. ($1 = 0.8600 euros)

item.title: Hermann equals ODI debut record as South Africa rout Namibia
item.description: South Africa opener Jordan Hermann equalled the record for the most runs on a One Day International debut with a blistering knock of 150 that saw his side overcome hosts Namibia in the first of their three-match series on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa opener Jordan Hermann equalled the record for the most runs on a One Day International debut with a blistering knock of 150 that saw his side overcome hosts Namibia in the first of their three-match series on Wednesday. South Africa, who were put in to bat, scored 348-6 off their 50 overs to win by 99 runs on the Duckworth–Lewis–Stern (DLS) method after rain interrupted Namibia’s reply and they finished with 162-8 off 31 overs, chasing a reduced target of 262. Hermann, one of three debutants in a weakened South African side, hit 20 boundaries, including three sixes, in his 126-ball knock, putting on 190 for the second wicket with Tony de Zorzi. He survived a run-out on 30 after an umpire’s error was not rectified because no television reviews were available, and his knock equalled the record set by teammate Matthew Breetzke last year, who also scored 150 on his ODI debut against New Zealand in a tri-series in Pakistan. Hermann raced from 100 to 150 in just 32 balls before being caught at cover off Ruben Trumpelmann, who was the pick of the home bowlers and claimed 4-68. Namibia were always behind the required run rate and their cause was made even more arduous when their innings was twice interrupted by rain. When they returned to the crease after the second delay, their target was reset to a near-impossible 167 runs off eight overs. Wednesday’s clash was the first ODI between the neighbours, who along with Zimbabwe co-host next year’s World Cup. They meet again at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Friday.

item.title: Tate brothers lose bid for release from US jail pending extradition
item.description: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate lost their bid for release from a Miami jail on Wednesday as they contest extradition to Britain, where they are wanted on rape charges.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate lost their bid for release from a [USN:L6N44411G TEXT:"Miami jail"] on Wednesday as they contest extradition to Britain, where they are wanted on rape charges. In denying bail for the [USN:L6N4440SP TEXT:"Tate brothers"], Miami-based U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis said the brothers' wealth and frequent international travel made them "quintessential flight risks." "While (the brothers) may not in fact possess what extravagant holdings they portray themselves as possessing online, the record reflects that they possess an exceptional capacity to flee the jurisdiction," Louis wrote. In a statement, the Tates' lawyers said they would "continue to defend themselves against the allegations they face and engage with the appropriate legal processes in each jurisdiction." In court filings, their lawyers had previously argued their "extraordinary public visibility" would make it impractical for them to flee, and described social media posts in which the brothers touted their wealth as "theatrical" and "grandiose." Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, were arrested in Miami on July 18 after Britain requested their extradition to face charges of rape, assault and facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. The Tate brothers, who have dual U.S. and British citizenship, have denied any wrongdoing. The arrests marked a new phase in the legal troubles for the former kickboxers, who have built a large online following promoting their views on masculinity and wealth. Andrew Tate has previously described himself as a misogynist. TATES SAY THEY PLAY CHARACTERS ONLINE Prosecutors with the Miami U.S. Attorney's office argued there was a strong presumption in favor of detention in international extradition cases. They said the brothers could pose a danger to the public if released, citing British allegations that they strangled victims during forcible rapes. The Tates recruited dozens of women to work for a webcam pornography business starting in 2014, and later ran online courses called "Hustler's University," prosecutors said in an August 10 court filing. At an [USN:L6N44O0VS TEXT:"August 27 hearing"] in Miami federal court, prosecutors showed the court a video of Andrew Tate saying "slap, slap, grab, choke, shut up bitch, sex." At the hearing, both Tate brothers testified they were playing characters online when they made crude remarks. Louis wrote on Wednesday that the nature of the allegations against the Tates indicated they posed dangers to the community. The brothers have also been under investigation on charges including human trafficking since 2022 in Romania, where they were mainly based since 2017. Romanian prosecutors [USN:L8N44W0FU TEXT:"officially indicted"] Andrew Tate on Friday on charges of trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering. Tristan Tate was indicted for complicity. A Romanian lawyer for the Tates said they rejected the allegations. BRITISH CHARGES SPAN SEVEN YEARS The legal process for determining whether the Tate brothers may be extradited to Britain could take months. Britain has until September 16 to submit its full extradition request to the State Department, U.S. court records show. The impetus for the brothers' arrests in Miami was new charges brought by Britain's Crown Prosecution Service relating to alleged offenses involving four alleged victims between July 2010 and August 2017. They had previously faced rape and human trafficking charges in Britain related to three alleged victims, the CPS said. A British judge issued a warrant for their arrests in 2024. They have not appeared in British court to enter a plea to those charges. Britain is seeking to extradite the brothers to face both sets of charges.

item.title: As forest loss accelerates, can the world meet the rising demand for wood?
item.description: With the impacts of climate change being felt across the globe, forests are under pressure as never before.
item.dc:creator: Angeli Mehta
item.content:encoded: With the impacts of climate change being felt across the globe, forests are under pressure as never before. While agriculture is the main driver of permanent deforestation, wildfires contributed 30% of tree cover loss and logging accounted for a 25% loss between 2001 and 2025, according to WRI. This loss may be temporary, but forests can take decades to recover and may never return to full health. Boreal forests have been ravaged to make toilet paper, while in Europe wood pellets are burned for energy. Five years after countries pledged to halt and reverse forest loss by 2030, there has been scant progress . At the same time demand for timber, which is expected to grow 37% by 2050 , could rise even higher if more wood is used for construction – a climate solution to replace demand for high-carbon steel and cement. Against this bleak backdrop, the most ambitious regulatory solution on offer is the EU’s deforestation regulation (EUDR), which will come into effect at the end of this year after twice being delayed. The question is, how much can it do to move the dial? Under the regulation, importers bringing a range of commodities including wood and paper products onto the European market (or exporting them from Europe) will have to prove they didn’t rely on recently deforested or degraded land. Operators and traders will have to provide the exact geo-coordinates of plots where commodities are sourced. For the 141 countries classed as low risk, including the UK and all EU countries, there will be less stringent checks. These include Romania, home to much of Europe’s old growth and primary forests, where NGO’s have called out a swathe of illegalities . A drone view shows a burnt forest affected by a wildfire in Le Temple, Gironde, France, July 29, 2026. Wildfires contributed 30% of tree cover loss between 2001 and 2025. REUTERS/Yves Herman Land that was classified as forest in 2020 can still be used for wood production, so long as it’s not converted into a plantation, for example. Since the EU relies on the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) definition of a forest as having at least 10% canopy cover, observers think enforcement could be challenging. By contrast, the U.N. Environment Programme definition is at least 30% canopy cover. Jack Hurd, head of earth systems at the World Economic Forum, points out that encroachment on forests is often insidious. “It's very rare that earth-moving equipment rocks up to the edge of a natural forest, and the next thing you know, it's clear-cut. Usually, there is a selective harvesting regime going on that's quasi-legal, and they take a few more trees than they're supposed to, and then the big firms move out and sell the concession to somebody who's a little bit more risk-tolerant and, all of a sudden, the forest starts to get degraded, and then more people are settling in that area, then eventually it gets cleared.” Leah Samberg is lead scientist at the Accountability Framework initiative, which advises companies on achieving and monitoring ethical supply chains. She says the difficulty of defining deforestation in the timber industry makes risk assessment, monitoring and verification critical. The AFI’s latest analysis of CDP’s disclosure data shows the largest proportion of companies disclosing deforestation risk (43%) are in the timber sector. But just 11% of timber disclosures report that more than 90% of their sourcing is deforestation-free. The EU has tried to cut deforestation in timber supply chains before, with the European Union Timber Regulation. But research by the Wyss Academy for Nature in Switzerland suggests that the EUTR substantially increased forest loss in the 52 most EU-trade dependent countries, between 2010 and 2019. Supply chains were restructured so timber was diverted to less regulated markets and the conversion of forests to agriculture accelerated, with nothing to stop those agricultural commodities being exported to the EU, the researchers said. With the EUDR, that door will be closed, but it can’t entirely prevent leakage, says the report’s author Stefano Jud. He points out that timber producers will be able to sell into China’s huge domestic market. “The Chinese only run into problems when they want to resell (after processing) to the EU.” An increase in demand for timber is being fuelled in part by its use in construction as an alternative to high-carbon steel and cement. REUTERS/Mike Blake The EUDR’s requirement for full supply-chain traceability, is particularly challenging for the global wood pellet industry. But researchers in the U.S. anticipate that the trade will largely shift to unregulated Asian markets , with only a slight fall in global production. “You need a global regime that avoids (these) kind of leakage effects (but) to be effective, you need to maintain those supply-chain relationships, because that's the way you can exert influence on the behaviour of producers.” That means building governance capacity in other countries, adds Jud. Samberg has no doubt that the EU regulation is a “net positive for deforestation-free action globally, (thanks to) the awareness and resources it’s brought to the problem”. However, she adds, “the narrow focus on supply chain compliance, as opposed to broader transformation in sourcing areas, creates incentives to clean up your own supply chain (but) not solve the problem”. It had been hoped EUDR would spur similar action in the markets where the EU sources the biggest volumes, and there is some evidence of progress. The UK has said it will enact legislation consistent with the EUDR across the same range of deforestation-risk commodities; China, which had raised security concerns about geolocation data, may now be exploring pathways for cooperation with Europe. And in Brazil, reports suggest that the country’s National Space Research Institute has developed technology to generate data at the granularity required by EUDR. Illegally logged timber is worth between $51 billion and $152 billion annually. REUTERS/Annegret Hilse In Europe, meanwhile, the EUDR’s data requirement has spawned a host of companies to help importers trace timber origins. When Netherlands-based timber trader Timberhub set up its managed marketplace to purchase and supply timber, it set out to ensure it could trace every piece of timber on its platform to a verified and legal source. Now it also offers EUDR compliance as a service, which has brought new customers from the pulp and paper industries. But co-founder Dimitris Pagkratis says the penalties European importers will face for breaching the EUDR “will always be a rounding error next to the volume of trade. The real effect is the trade that quietly stops happening – illegal logging, and it is genuinely hard to size.” Interpol gauges trade in illegally logged timber is worth between $51 billion and $152 billion annually , while Client Earth estimates 20% of it ends up in the EU. “We are regulating a flow that nobody currently measures well,” observes Pagkratis. Subhra Bhattacharjee, director general of the Forest Stewardship Council, agrees that the EUDR is no cure-all. “Deforestation is a very complex problem, requiring measures coming at it from different angles with all kinds of actors involved – local, international, regional,” she says. “EUDR is addressing it from the demand side, at the same time, you need the supply side; the policing on the ground.” Over 175 million hectares of forest is certified by the FSC, through over 1,700 forest management and 70,000 chain of custody certificates. But certification doesn’t mean compliance with the EUDR. The FSC has been trying to build capacity to meet EUDR amongst its certificate holders by “turning it into a workable, applicable, practicable set of instructions for companies”, Bhattacharjee says. While companies, investors and consumers rely on certification, there are numerous reports of wood being certified as FSC when it’s not. Last year, FSC members voted for a motion, tabled by NGOs and corporates, to assess what would be required to develop a global digital system for traceability and volume control within FSC-certified supply chains. A roadmap to implement the system by 2030 is due by the end of next year. A worker moves wood chips with a digger at a pulp mill. REUTERS/Michael Buholzer Some geolocation data is already being collected as part of a voluntary regulatory module for due diligence and risk assessments to meet EUDR. One solution to deforestation risk promoted by the pulp and paper industry is to plant fast-growing hardwood species such as eucalyptus, particularly on the millions of hectares of land that have already been degraded by intensive cattle farming or agriculture. Read more Environmental groups have long criticised large-scale eucalyptus plantations for their impacts on water resources, biodiversity and soils, though this is mainly where they replace natural forest ecosystems. Brazil-based Suzano is the world’s largest pulp producer, and a big player in the paper and packaging industry. Its pulp is derived from eucalyptus plantations, occupying land that was once degraded pasture. The company stresses that it takes a broad watershed approach and selects its trees to suit different growing conditions. It’s had a zero-deforestation commitment since 2020, backed up by geolocation and traceability programmes. Paulo Leime, managing director for Suzano’s operations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, says that around Suzano’s 1.6 million hectares of plantations sit another 1.1m hectares of land that is being protected to allow it to regenerate. Having natural forest around plantations allows better management of watersheds, and has brought valuable knowledge about which insects can be used instead of chemicals to combat pests. Brazil-based Suzano derives its pulp from eucalyptus plantations, occupying land that was once degraded pasture. Suzano/Handout via REUTERS “There is a business case for sustainability,” he says. “We plant a tree. It takes seven years to grow. We have to be looking to the next decades’ strategy to make sure we are taking care of the environment where we operate and the communities around that.” Suzano is exploring a business model to finance restoration through the sale of carbon credits, in a venture with Rabobank, Santander, food company Marfrig and mining group Vale. Its first project, announced last year, aims to restore 1,200 hectares of Atlantic forest on land owned by another eucalyptus pulp producer, Veracel Celulose. “Our biggest challenge with EUDR was how to build technology to make sure this information flowed according to the customers, because it's a very complex value chain,” says Leime. “If we include our operations, our customers’ operations, which will then sell to (others), how do you make sure this is traceable from the very beginning until the very end.” Suzano’s answer has been to develop a proprietary system to demonstrate EUDR compliance, something that is bringing new business.
